items.q: The city our Beloved Prophet ﷺ migrated to, earlier called Yathrib.
The Muslims of Madinah who welcomed the emigrants.
The Muslims who migrated from Makkah.
The first great battle of Islam, in 2 AH / 624 CE.
The battle at the mountain near Madinah in 3 AH / 625 CE.
The battle in which the Muslims dug a trench around Madinah.
The Companion who suggested digging the trench.
The treaty with Quraysh in 6 AH / 628 CE.
The opening of Makkah took place in this year.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ made the Muhajirun and Ansar brothers; this is called this.
The direction of prayer was changed to this.
Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in this year.
The farewell pilgrimage took place in this year.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ passed away in this year.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ passed away at this age.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ passed away in the room of this wife.
The first caliph after our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The uncle of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ martyred at Uhud.
The first Friday prayer of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ in Madinah was with this tribe, on the way from Quba'.
The first muezzin of Islam.
The mountain of which our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said, "It loves us and we love it" (meaning).
The two grandsons of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, sons of our lady Fatimah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا).
items.a: Our masters al-Hasan and al-Husayn (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا)

items.q: The Muslims faced this city in prayer before the Qiblah changed.
The wife of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ who was the daughter of our master 'Umar (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ).
The number of Muslims at Badr, roughly.
The Quraysh leader and fiercest enemy of our Beloved Master ﷺ, killed at Badr.
Badr took place in this month.
Badr is called this in the Qur'an, "the day of the criterion" (meaning).
The archers at Uhud were told to stay on this hill.
The Quraysh commander who attacked from behind at Uhud, later a great Companion.
The Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah was meant to last this many years.
The Pledge under the tree at al-Hudaybiyah.
The Companion sent to Makkah as envoy before the pledge.
The Quraysh envoy who agreed the treaty terms with our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The Jewish fortress town conquered in 7 AH / 628 CE.
The Companion given the banner at Khaybar.
items.a: Our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The battle in 8 AH / 629 CE where three commanders were martyred in turn.
The three commanders at Mu'tah.
items.a: Zayd ibn Harithah, our master Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِم)

items.q: The Companion called "Sayf Allah" (the Sword of Allah) after Mu'tah.
The battle after the opening of Makkah, in the valley near Ta'if.
The last expedition of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, in 9 AH / 630 CE.
The year of delegations, when many tribes came to accept Islam.
The place of the Farewell Sermon.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ was buried here.
items.a: In the room of our lady 'A'ishah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا)

items.q: The Qiblah changed after the Muslims had faced Jerusalem in Madinah for this many months.
The month of the Battle of Uhud.
Apart from the 'umrah joined to His ﷺ Hajj, our Beloved Prophet ﷺ made all His ﷺ 'umrahs in this month.
The 'umrah made the year after al-Hudaybiyah, as the treaty allowed.
The son of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ born in Madinah, who died as an infant.
items.a: Our master Ibrahim, son of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ

items.q: The first mosque built in Madinah city by our Beloved Prophet ﷺ Himself ﷺ.
The covered area of the mosque where poor Companions lived.
The agreement setting out the rights of Madinah's communities.
The number of Quraysh killed at Badr.
The number of Muslims martyred at Uhud.
The hypocrite leader who withdrew a third of the army before Uhud.
The woman Companion who defended our Beloved Prophet ﷺ at Uhud with a sword.
The confederate army at the Trench numbered about this many.
The Jewish tribe that broke its treaty during the Trench.
The Companion whose judgement was accepted on Banu Qurayzah.
The first Jewish tribe expelled from Madinah, after Badr.
The Jewish tribe expelled after it plotted to kill our Beloved Master ﷺ, in 4 AH / 625 CE.
The surah revealed about the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir.
The Muslim army at the opening of Makkah numbered about this many.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said whoever enters this man's house is safe, at the opening of Makkah.
The number of idols around the Ka'bah removed at the opening.
The verse recited as idols fell: "Truth has come and falsehood has vanished" (meaning).
The Companion who gave the call to prayer on top of the Ka'bah.
The Companion who, in a famous report, gave half his wealth when our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) gave all.
items.a: Our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The Companion who equipped a large part of the army of Tabuk.
The Quraysh army at Badr numbered about this many.
Some captives of Badr could earn their freedom by teaching ten Muslim children this.
The Quraysh army at Uhud numbered about this many.
The number of archers placed on the hill at Uhud.
The Companion who commanded the archers at Uhud.
The Companion who carried the Muslims' banner at Uhud until he was martyred.
The three Companions who stayed behind from Tabuk and were forgiven in Surah al-Tawbah.
items.a: Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', Hilal ibn Umayyah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِم)

items.q: The Companion whose long narration tells the story of the three who stayed behind.
The number of days the three who stayed behind from Tabuk were boycotted.
The Quraysh trade caravan at Badr was led by this man, who later accepted Islam.
The shelter built for our Beloved Prophet ﷺ to command from at Badr.
The Companion who advised camping near the water at Badr.
The daughter of our Beloved Master ﷺ who died while the army was at Badr.
After our lady Ruqayyah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا), our master 'Uthman (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) married this daughter, and was called "Dhul-Nurayn".
items.a: Our lady Umm Kulthum (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا)

items.q: The Companion who killed our master Hamzah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) at Uhud before he accepted Islam.
The Companion of Hudaybiyah who came in chains and was returned under the treaty.
The Companion who later formed a group on the coast, attacking Quraysh caravans, after Hudaybiyah.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ sent letters to rulers after Hudaybiyah; the Byzantine emperor was this.
The Persian emperor who tore up our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ letter.
The ruler of Egypt who sent gifts in reply.
The Companion who carried the letter to Heraclius.
The Quraysh leader whom Heraclius questioned about our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
Our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ seal ring read this.
The Muslims at Hunayn were at first pleased by this, then fled.
The Companion who shouted to the Ansar at Hunayn to rally them.
items.a: Our master al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The Companion appointed to lead the Hajj in 9 AH / 631 CE.
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The Companion who said at Badr, "We will not say as the people of Musa (عليه السلام) said, 'Go, you and your Lord'" (paraphrased).
The two young Ansari Companions who struck Abu Jahl at Badr shared this first name.
The army of Tabuk numbered about this many.
The Companion sent after our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) in 9 AH to announce the opening of Surah Bara'ah.
items.a: Our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The Companion who taught the Qur'an in Yemen and was told "How will you judge?" (paraphrased).
The last army our Beloved Master ﷺ prepared, sent after His ﷺ death by our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ).
items.a: The army of Usamah ibn Zayd (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا)

items.q: Usamah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) was about this age when he led it.
The month in which our Beloved Prophet ﷺ passed away.
The day of the week our Beloved Prophet ﷺ passed away.
The place where the Ansar met after our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ passing and chose our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ).
The Companion who said, "Whoever worshipped Muhammad ﷺ, Muhammad ﷺ has died..." (meaning) and recited 3:144.
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The Muslims at Hudaybiyah numbered about this many.
The Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah was broken by Quraysh's allies attacking this tribe.
The tribe of Quraysh's allies who attacked Khuza'ah.
The Companion who wrote to warn Quraysh of the march on Makkah and was forgiven as a man of Badr.
items.a: Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The surah revealed about the letter of Hatib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ), opening "Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies" (meaning).
The battle of the Trench is also called this in the Qur'an.
The Companion who went out alone at night to spy on the Confederates.
The expedition in which the verse of tayammum came down, by one view.
items.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tayammum (Fath al-Bari)

items.q: The Companion whose death made the Throne shake, as our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said (paraphrased).
The Companion who led our Beloved Prophet's ﷺ funeral bathing, with al-'Abbas and others.
items.a: Our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)
items.src: Sunan Abi Dawud; Sirat Ibn Hisham

items.q: The expedition named after the rags the Companions wrapped round their wounded feet.
The well where about seventy Qur'an reciters were martyred in 4 AH / 625 CE.
The Companion, captured after al-Raji', who prayed two rak'ahs before Quraysh put him to death.
While Ka'b ibn Malik (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) was boycotted, the king of this land wrote inviting him to join him.
The son of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy who was a sincere Companion and stood against his father.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said to Quraysh at the opening of Makkah: "Go, you are free" (meaning); this freedom is called this.
items.src: Sirat Ibn Hisham; wording to be checked

items.q: The Companion of Badr who was the first to die in Madinah from the Muhajirun, by one view, and was kissed by our Beloved Master ﷺ.
items.a: Our master 'Uthman ibn Maz'un (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)
items.src: Sunan Abi Dawud; to be checked
